cards.question: Where do I start?
cards.answer:
I recommend setting up the **Vault** before entering any data. Search for *Vault* on this page to read the Vault guides.

Once the Vault is set up, I recommend going in this order:

1. Add your services and prices in [Services](app:services).
2. Add the payment methods from the [Works](app:works) list.
3. Add memory cards and backup locations in [Storage](app:storage/cards), to keep track of what you use in your works and where you save the photos.
4. Add a customer in [Customers](app:customers).
5. Record your first work in [Works](app:works), choosing the customer and the services you have just created.

Once you have a few works recorded, the [Dashboard](app:dashboard) shows you the summary of everything.

cards.question: What must exist before I record a work?
cards.answer:
To record a work you need two things that must already exist, because in the work you pick them from a list:

- the **customer**, which you create in [Customers](app:customers)
- the **services**, which you create in [Services](app:services)

If you cannot find the customer or the service you need, it simply has not been created yet: no need to start over, add it and then continue the work from [Works](app:works).
keywords: what do I need before a work

cards.question: What do I see on the Dashboard?
cards.answer:
The [Dashboard](app:dashboard) is your summary: it shows the **recent works** and the **payments to receive**, so you see at once what you need to follow up without opening every work.

When you need the detail, open [Works](app:works) or [Customers](app:customers).

cards.question: How do I add a customer?
cards.answer:
In the [Customers](app:customers) page, the **Add Customer** button opens the form where you collect your customers' people and contacts, which you then choose in your works.

Write the name and the details you have, then press **Create Customer**. You do not need to fill everything in right away: you can complete the form when you have the information. I recommend entering email and phone as soon as you have them, so you find them when you need to contact the customer.

If the customer is a couple or a family, enter the people in the same customer: you will find the explanation in the guide about two people.

Once you have set up the Vault, personal data (email, phone, address) is protected: to read or edit it the Vault must be unlocked.

cards.question: How do I put two people in the same customer, like a couple?
cards.answer: In the customer page you can add more people with the **Add Person** button.
keywords: add a person to a customer

cards.question: Why can't I delete a customer?
cards.answer:
A customer linked to works cannot be deleted. If you want to delete the customer, the delete window shows the linked works: open them and change the customer, or delete the works and then delete the customer.

Whatever you delete goes to the [Bin](app:trash), where you can get it back.

cards.question: How do I create a service and its price?
cards.answer:
Go to [Services](app:services) and press **Add Service**. Write the name, the base price and, if you like, some notes, then press **Create Service**.

When you select the service in a work, you can change the price for that work only (examples: a discount, or a service with a higher cost), without changing the general price on the service.
keywords: change the price in a work

cards.question: How do I record a new work?
cards.answer:
Go to [Works](app:works) and create a new work. Fill in, in order:

- the **title** and the **date** of the work
- the **customer**
- the **services included**
- the **installments** of the payment

Then press **Create Work**. At least one service and one installment are needed.

cards.question: How do I record the installments and payments of a work?
cards.answer:
In the work, in the payments section, press **Add Installment** for each expected payment: amount, date and payment method.

The installments together must cover exactly the price of the services, otherwise the work will not save. When a customer pays, remember to mark the installment as paid.
keywords: installments do not cover the price

cards.question: What do Paid, Partial and Unpaid mean?
cards.answer:
The payment status of a work is a summary of the payment status of the installments you saved. Read the status this way:

- **Paid**: all the installments have already been paid to you
- **Partial**: some installments are still to be paid
- **Unpaid**: no installment has been paid yet

Check and update the status of the installments in every work to keep track of your transactions flawlessly: it will be essential as a summary.

cards.question: How do I add a payment method, like bank transfer or cash?
cards.answer:
In the [Works](app:works) list, click the button at the top right, **Manage payment types**: enter the name of the method (*Bank transfer*, *PayPal*, *Cash* and so on) and save.

You write the names yourself, so you can use the ones you really use with your customers.

Inside each work, in the **Payments** section, when you enter the payment installments (for example *Deposit* and *Balance*) you choose the method and the payment date.

cards.question: Can I attach documents to a work?
cards.answer:
Yes. In the work, in the **Files** section, you can upload PDFs, documents and images, or add an external link. Each file can have a name of your choice, which does not overwrite the real name of the file you uploaded: it is only a label to sum up the content of the file or the external link.

Once you have set up the Vault, files are protected, so to upload or open them the Vault must be unlocked.

cards.question: How do I record shots taken and photos delivered in a work?
cards.answer:
In every work, in the **Shots** section, you can enter the **Shots taken** (how many you made) and the **Photos delivered** (how many you gave the client).

These numbers are optional: if you leave them empty no number is saved and the work does not appear in the [Shots History](app:storage/shots).

Check the numbers: the photos delivered cannot be more than the shots taken.
keywords: how many shots did I take
you delivered more photos than you took

cards.question: How do I keep track of photo delivery in a work?
cards.answer:
In the work you find the **Delivery** section, where you can note how you delivered the work to the client (a gallery link, a transfer, a USB stick).

- **Delivery title**: a name to recognise it, for example the name of the Pixieset gallery.
- **Link**: the gallery address. You must enter a valid URL: if the system does not detect a real web address, it warns you before saving.
- **Link expiry date**: the date until which the link works. It is a note for you and goes into the message for the client: the CRM **does not alert you** and does not switch the link off, so renew the gallery in time. Leave the field empty if there is no expiry.
- **Gallery password** and **Delivery notes**: the gallery password, if any, and whatever you want to remember. With the Vault they are protected like the other private texts: you read and edit them only while the CRM is unlocked.

cards.question: How do I prepare the message with the link for the client?
cards.answer:
In the **Delivery** section of the work press **Copy message**: the text is copied and you paste it wherever you like (WhatsApp, email, social).

- The message says *Hi*, followed by the first name of the main contact of the customer, and contains the link.
- If you wrote the password and the expiry date, it adds them.
- The button stays off until you write a link: with a USB stick there is nothing to send.
- With the Vault locked the password cannot be read, so it does not go into the message: remember to unlock the Vault before copying.
keywords: message for the client with the gallery

cards.question: How do I keep track of my memory cards?
cards.answer:
In the [Storage](app:storage/cards) section you can enter all the **Memory Cards** you own: save them with descriptive names that help you recognise them.

In the **Memory Cards** section press the button at the top right, **Add Card**, type the **Card Name** (for example *SD-A 128GB SanDisk*) and press **Create Card**.

Every new memory card is saved as *Ready*. The other statuses are *In use*, *Backed Up* and *Damaged*. The status becomes *In use* when the card is put in a work.

I recommend changing the status of the cards in the single work: once you have made the backup, open the work and tick **Backup Done**. If you have already formatted the card, also tick **Formatting Done**. When a card receives both the backup and the formatting, it goes back to *Ready* and you can use it in other works.

A card that is *In use* cannot be put in other works. In the card list you see which work it is currently used in: open it and tick **Backup Done** and **Formatting Done**.

When you set a card as *Damaged*, it stays in the works where it was already used, but it cannot be used in other works.

Every time a card changes status you see the date and time of the change, to remind you when you made the backup, when you formatted it or when you marked it as *Damaged*.

cards.question: How do backup locations work (where I keep my photos)?
cards.answer:
**Backup locations** are the places where you keep the files of your works, for example an external drive, a NAS or the cloud.

Keeping track of where you save your backups helps you quickly find where you saved the photos of each work, without having to remember it. From the [Storage](app:storage/backups) page, **Backup Locations** section, you add them with the **Add Backup Location** button.

What you can enter:

- **Name**: the only required field. Use a name that lets you recognise the drive at a glance (example: *Synology NAS, office*).
- **Type** and **Capacity**: free fields (for example *SSD* and *4 TB*). They are notes for you: the gestionale does not check the space left, so keep them up to date yourself.
- **Status**: **Active** (you still use it), **Full** (no more space but the files stay there) or **Retired** (you no longer use it). It blocks nothing: it is used by the filters, for example to see right away which drives still have room.
- **Notes**: anything you want to remember, for example where the drive is kept. Once you have set up the Vault, you read and edit them only with the gestionale unlocked.

From the location list you also see how many works you saved in that location. Opening a single location you see the list of all the works saved there.

Thanks to this information it only takes a few seconds to find where you saved a work: open the work from the [Works](app:works) list and look at the **Storage & Backup** section.

I recommend updating the **Status** (*Full* or *Retired*) when a drive fills up, so you do not pick it for the next work.
keywords: what to write in type and capacity

cards.question: What do the statuses of a card mean and how do they change?
cards.answer:
Every memory card has a status, which tells you at a glance where it stands and whether you can use it for a new work:

- **Ready**: it is free, you can put it in a work.
- **In Use**: it is in a work and holds the photos still to be copied.
- **Backed Up**: the photos have been copied, but the card is not formatted yet: do not reuse it until you have.
- **Damaged**: you no longer want to use it, so it does not appear among the cards you can choose in works.

A card is linked to **one work at a time**, the last one you put it in: this is why it cannot end up in two works together. Older works that still list it are history and never change its status again.

**From the work to the card** (when you save the work): a *Ready* card put in the work becomes *In Use*. With **Backup Done** it becomes *Backed Up*. If you also tick **Formatting Done** it goes back to *Ready* (it stays listed in the work, but you can already use it in another one). If you untick one and save, the card steps back one step.

**From the card to the work**: if you change the **Status** of a card in Storage, the work it is used in updates too. **Backup Done** is ticked by itself only when all its cards (not damaged) have the backup; **Formatting Done** only when they are all *Ready*. If a card goes back, the tick is removed.

**Damaged**: the card stays in the work with that status and does not count for the ticks. It stays *Damaged* even if you remove it from the work or delete the work. If you repair it or want to use it again, remember to set it back to *Ready* by hand.

cards.question: How do I find where I saved the backup of a work?
cards.answer:
To find where you saved a work you have two ways:

- From the [Works](app:works) list, open the work and scroll down to the **Storage & Backup** section to see where you saved it.
- From the [Backup Locations](app:storage/backups) list, open one location at a time and scroll down to the **Works** section, where you can look for the work.

I recommend the first option: it is faster to search for the work and see where you saved it, rather than searching through all the locations.
keywords: where did I save the photos
find the backup of a work
which drive is the work on
where are the photos of a work
which works are on this drive

cards.question: How do I read and filter the card list?
cards.answer:
The card list in [Storage](app:storage/cards) shows you which cards are in use and in which works they are used.

A card with the *Ready* status is free: either it is new, or the backup and the formatting have already been done, so you can use it in another work.

If you want to quickly see which cards need a backup, click the **In use** filter and you will see only the cards that are active in a work. Next to each *In use* card you see the work it is in: open it and check whether you still have to make the backup and format the card.

When you tick **Backup Done** and **Formatting Done**, the card goes back to *Ready* and you can use it in other works.
keywords: which work is the card in

cards.question: How do I note where a work is saved, and what does the red warning mean?
cards.answer:
To note where you saved a work, open it and in the **Storage & Backup** section press **Add Backup Location**, then pick a location from the list.

- You can add **more than one** (for example external drive and cloud), but the same location cannot be chosen twice.
- Use the arrows to reorder rows and the red bin to remove a row. Then remember to save the work.
- If the location does not exist yet, use **Create a new backup location**: it opens in another tab, so you do not lose what you are typing.

**Red warning**: it means a chosen location was **deleted** or is in the Bin, so that work no longer has a safe place noted. In the [Works](app:works) list the work has a red circle with a triangle, and the **Works with warnings** button shows only the ones to fix. In the work the row is outlined in red: choose another location or remove the row and save. Otherwise restore the location from the [Bin](app:trash).
keywords: assign a location to a work
storage and backup in the work
how to remove the work warning

cards.question: How do I use cards inside a work?
cards.answer:
In the single work, **Memory Cards** section, you say which cards you use for the shoot: this way the gestionale updates the status of each card and tells you which ones you still have to back up.

Remember to save the work: card statuses update only when you save.

Press the **Add Card** button, choose from the list and, if you like, write a note. You can use several cards in the same work. The list shows only *Ready* cards: if you see *No cards available*, add a card in [Storage](app:storage/cards) or free one of those in use. Once you have set up the Vault, the notes are protected: with the gestionale locked they cannot be read.

When you have made the backup and formatted all the cards of the work, click **Backup Done** and **Formatting Done**. Formatting can be ticked only after the backup. The cards then go back to *Ready* to be used in other works.

Every time the status of a card changes, you see the date and time of the change next to the card in the work. To take a card out of the work use the red bin: when you save, the card goes back to *Ready* (it stays *Damaged* if it was).

When you delete a work, the cards in use go back to *Ready* even if you had not made the backup and formatted them. I recommend always checking first that the photos are safe. If you restore the work from the [Bin](app:trash), the cards stay free and do not reconnect by themselves.
keywords: add a card to a work
delete a work and its cards

cards.question: How does the Shots History work?
cards.answer:
In [Storage](app:storage/backups), in the **Shots History** tab, you see how many shots you took and how many photos you delivered, work by work: useful to understand how the year went. Each row shows **Work** (the title opens the work), **Date**, **Shots taken** and **Photos delivered**. You write the numbers yourself inside each work.

- **Year**: above the table choose the year (or **All years**). The year of the work date counts and only years that have counts are offered.
- **Totals**: on the right you read **Works**, **Shots taken** and **Photos delivered** of what you are looking at. A missing number counts as zero.
- **Yellow triangle**: for that work you wrote more photos delivered than shots, usually it is a typing mistake. Open the work and check: it is only a hint, it blocks nothing.
- **Missing work or empty history**: only works with at least one of the two numbers appear (otherwise you read *No shot counts yet*), so to see a work fill in its numbers in the **Shots** section. A work without a valid date appears only under **All years**.
keywords: how many shots did I take
how many photos delivered this year

cards.question: How do I use cards during a shoot, step by step?
cards.answer:
Here is how to use cards in a shoot, from start to finish. By following these steps the status of each card always tells you whether you can reuse it or whether it still holds photos to save.

1. Add your cards in [Storage](app:storage/cards): you do it only once.
2. Before the shoot open the work, in the **Memory Cards** section choose the ones you take and save: they become *In Use*.
3. After the shoot copy the photos, tick **Backup Done** and save: they become *Backed Up*. Do not reuse them yet.
4. Format the cards, tick **Formatting Done** and save: they go back to *Ready*. They stay listed in the work as history, but you can already use them in another one.

If a card breaks, mark it **Damaged** from the card: this way you do not pick it by mistake and it no longer counts for the work's ticks.
keywords: how do I organise my cards

cards.question: How do I delete a card and get it back?
cards.answer:
To delete a card, open it in [Storage](app:storage/cards), press **Delete** and confirm. It is not gone for good: it goes to the [Bin](app:trash) and you can restore it from there (in Storage a small **Bin** button appears when there is something inside).

- **If it is In Use it cannot be deleted**: you see *Card is currently in use and cannot be deleted*, because it still holds photos to save. Remove the card from the work, or complete backup and formatting, then try again.
- **In works**: a deleted card also disappears from the **Memory Cards** section of the works where it was written, and if you restore it you see it again. If you need it to stay listed in a work, do not delete it while you still need it.

cards.question: How do I see my works in the calendar?
cards.answer:
Open [Calendar](app:calendar): each work appears on the day of its date, and pressing a work opens it.

To tell your works apart at a glance you can choose the colour of each one in the **Calendar Color** section of the work: for example one colour for weddings and another for portrait sessions.

cards.question: What is the Vault and what does it protect?
cards.answer:
The Vault is a password lock that protects your customers' data: names, contacts, addresses, notes, work titles and attached documents. As long as you do not unlock it, this data cannot be read, even by someone who manages to get into the site.

I recommend setting up the Vault first of all, before entering any data in the gestionale. Go to [Settings](app:settings), Vault section, and click **Set Up Vault**.

Pay close attention to the messages you see on screen. The setup requires:

- creating a **password** to unlock the gestionale (keep it in a safe place)
- setting up an **authenticator** app, for example Google Authenticator ([iOS](https://apps.apple.com/app/google-authenticator/id388497605) and [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.authenticator2))
- saving the **recovery phrase** (you need it if you no longer remember your password: keep it in a safe place)
- saving the **recovery code** (you need it if you no longer remember your password: keep it in a safe place)

It may seem like "too much" security, but you will see that unlocking the gestionale when you need to work is very quick, and the safety and protection of the data are worth more than the 30 seconds needed to unlock the Vault. If you have a device that unlocks with a fingerprint (Mac, laptops or latest-generation keyboards) you can set up your fingerprint for a safe and very fast unlock.

For extra security, every time you step away from your device you can click **Lock Vault**, at the bottom left of the gestionale. The Vault also locks by itself after 15 minutes of inactivity.
keywords: how do I set up the vault

cards.question: I forgot the Vault password, what do I do?
cards.answer: No panic: on the unlock screen choose the option for a forgotten password and enter the **recovery phrase** or the **recovery code** from your recovery kit. Then you set a new password.

cards.question: Can I unlock the Vault with my fingerprint?
cards.answer:
Yes, on devices that allow it. After you have set up the Vault (when you have set the password and the authenticator app), in [Settings](app:settings), in the Vault section, you will see the **Turn on fingerprint unlock** option for that device: the password and the code are needed only once, to turn it on.

Once the feature is on you can unlock the Vault in a few seconds, without typing the password and without opening the authenticator app.

Anyone who can unlock that device can open the Vault from it: turn it on only on devices that you use yourself. If the device does not support it, the option does not appear and you keep using the password.

cards.question: What changed in the latest version?
cards.answer:
The gestionale tells you when there is a new update to install, which fixes bugs or adds or improves features.

Every time you update you will find a message on screen that explains what has changed or been fixed in each section.

You can read again the history of the changes of every update by opening the [Changelog](app:changelog): you also reach it by clicking the version number at the bottom left of the screen (for example *CRM 1.7.2*).

cards.question: How do I download a backup of my data?
cards.answer:
In [Settings](app:settings), in the **Backups** section, press **Download encrypted backup**: you get a file with the data of your CRM, protected.

The Vault must be on to do it. I recommend keeping the file and your recovery kit somewhere safe, away from the site, and making a new backup every now and then: that way, if something goes wrong, you always have a recent copy.

cards.question: How do I restore a backup?
cards.answer:
Open [Restore from a backup](app:restore). Choose a backup already saved on this site or upload the file, then enter the password, code or recovery phrase asked for.

Before writing anything, the CRM shows you what will change, and you can undo the latest restore. Be careful with the "replace everything" option: it cannot be undone, but a safety backup is made first.

cards.question: I deleted something by mistake, how do I get it back?
cards.answer:
No worries: open the [Bin](app:trash). You find the deleted items, with the date when they will disappear. Press **Restore item** to get them back, or **Delete for good** if you really want to remove them.

A customer or a service still used by a work cannot be deleted for good: first open the work and change the customer or the service, or delete the work.
